proposals.before: His father Yin had been junior mentor to the heir apparent and left chief clerk of the Secretariat.
proposals.after: His father Yin had been junior mentor to the heir apparent and left chief clerk of the Minister over the Masses.
proposals.reason: 司徒 is Situ (Minister over the Masses), not the Secretariat.

proposals.before: His father Yin was Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and Left Chief Clerk of the Secretariat.
proposals.after: His father Yin was Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and Left Chief Clerk of the Minister over the Masses.
proposals.reason: 司徒 is Situ, not the Secretariat.

proposals.before: Before the prince took government into his own hands, he left all affairs to his chief clerk Zhang Shao.
proposals.after: Before the prince took government into his own hands, he left all affairs to his adjutant Zhang Shao.
proposals.reason: 司馬 is the adjutant Sima, not 主簿 'chief clerk'.

proposals.before: Before the Taizu personally administered government affairs, all administration was entrusted to Chief Clerk Zhang Shao.
proposals.after: Before the Taizu personally administered government affairs, all administration was entrusted to Adjutant Zhang Shao.
proposals.reason: 司馬 should not be rendered Chief Clerk.

proposals.before: Once they met in the city. Dazzled by the sun, Hua did not recognize Shao and told his attendants, "That procession is enormous—it must be the prince himself going out."
proposals.after: Once they met in the city. Hua pretended not to know it was Shao and told his attendants, "That procession is enormous—it must be the prince himself going out."
proposals.reason: 陽不知 is 佯不知 'feigned ignorance', not sunlight dazzling Hua.

proposals.before: Once they met within the city. Hua in the sunlight did not recognize Shao and said to his attendants, "That guard procession is very grand—it must be the Prince going out."
proposals.after: Once they met within the city. Hua pretended not to know it was Shao and said to his attendants, "That guard procession is very grand—it must be the Prince going out."
proposals.reason: 陽不知 means pretended not to know, not 'in the sunlight'.

proposals.before: The prince led the civil and military officers of his headquarters and province under strict guard. Officials sent from the court could not approach his ranks. Army adviser Zhu Rongzi stood outside the Pingcheng gate with his sword in his arms and did not unbuckle his belt for several tens of days.
proposals.after: The prince led the civil and military officers of his headquarters and province under strict guard. Officials sent from the court could not approach his ranks. Army adviser Zhu Rongzi stood outside the cabin door of the imperial barge with his sword in his arms and did not unbuckle his belt for several tens of days.
proposals.reason: 平乘戶 is the cabin door of a large imperial vessel, not a place named Pingcheng.

proposals.before: He led the military and civil officials of the headquarters and province in strict array to guard themselves. The various officials dispatched from the court—all could not draw near his ranks. Army Adviser Zhu Rongzi embraced his sword outside the Pingcheng gate, not unbuckling his belt for several tens of days.
proposals.after: He led the military and civil officials of the headquarters and province in strict array to guard themselves. The various officials dispatched from the court—all could not draw near his ranks. Army Adviser Zhu Rongzi embraced his sword outside the door of the pingcheng barge, not unbuckling his belt for several tens of days.
proposals.reason: Literal 平乘戶外 is the barge doorway, not Pingcheng gate.

proposals.before: The emperor grieved deeply for him. Zhou Qiu, an attendant gentleman of the secretariat, said at his side, "When the Wang house is about to decline, the worthy perish first."
proposals.after: The emperor grieved deeply for him. Zhou Qiu, a secretariat drafter, said at his side, "When the Wang house is about to decline, the worthy perish first."
proposals.reason: 中書舍人 is the office of secretariat drafter (zhongshu sheren), not 'attendant gentleman of the secretariat', which confuses it with a different gentleman-attendant title.

proposals.before: His younger son Sengqian, at the end of the Qi Shengming era, served as minister president of the secretariat.
proposals.after: His younger son Sengqian, at the end of the Shengming era, served as minister president of the secretariat.
proposals.reason: 昇明 is the Liu Song Shengming era of Emperor Shun (AD 477–479), not a Qi reign; the idiomatic English invents 'Qi'.

proposals.before: In the sixth year Lady Su died. The emperor went in person to mourn at her bier and issued an edict: "From early on I have known partial bereavement, and my feelings are all the more ordinary. I have long wished to honor a worthy kinswoman and give some small expression to boundless grief.
proposals.after: In the sixth year Lady Su died. The emperor went in person to mourn at her bier and issued an edict: "From early on I have suffered the partial bereavement of losing a parent, and my feelings go beyond the ordinary. I have long wished to honor a worthy kinswoman and give some small expression to boundless grief.
proposals.reason: 情事兼常 means the feelings exceed the ordinary; 'all the more ordinary' reverses 兼常.

proposals.before: After his mother's mourning and burial, he was recalled as general of the palace garrison but firmly declined.
proposals.after: While he was in mourning for his mother, after the burial was completed, he was recalled as general of the palace garrison but firmly declined.
proposals.reason: 丁母憂，葬竟 is burial during mourning, not mourning's end; 服闋 is only in s0144.

proposals.before: The Taizu's birth mother Empress Zhang had died early; the Emperor served Su, whom the Empress Dowager had borne, very carefully.
proposals.after: Taizu's birth mother Empress Zhang had died early; the Emperor served Lady Su, a kinswoman connected with the Empress Dowager, with great care.
proposals.reason: Later 階緣戚屬 treats Su as a relative by kinship; 'whom the Empress Dowager had borne' over-commits to a daughter reading.

proposals.before: He served as chief clerk to the commandery prince, was recruited as an attendant administrative officer of the province, became chief clerk of the western bureau, was recommended as outstanding talent, and was magistrate of Jiaxing, winning a name for ability.
proposals.after: The commandery appointed him chief clerk; he was recruited as an attendant administrative officer of the province, became chief clerk of the western bureau, was recommended as outstanding talent, and was magistrate of Jiaxing, winning a name for ability.
proposals.reason: 郡命主簿 means the commandery appointed him as chief clerk, not service to a commandery prince.

proposals.before: Chief Clerk to the commandery prince, recruited as Attendant Administrative Officer of the province, Western Bureau Chief Clerk, recommended as Outstanding Talent, magistrate of Jiaxing—with a reputation for ability.
proposals.after: The commandery appointed him Chief Clerk; he was recruited as Attendant Administrative Officer of the province, Western Bureau Chief Clerk, recommended as Outstanding Talent, magistrate of Jiaxing—with a reputation for ability.
proposals.reason: 郡命 is an appointment by the commandery, not a prince.

proposals.before: He entered court as libationer of the secretariat, then served Prince Nanqian Yixuan as chief clerk of the left army and as magistrate of Qiantang, again with a strong record in office.
proposals.after: He entered court as libationer to the Minister of Education (Situ), then served Prince Nanqian Yixuan as chief clerk of the left army and as magistrate of Qiantang, again with a strong record in office.
proposals.reason: 司徒祭酒 is an office under the Situ, not the imperial secretariat.

proposals.before: He again became chief clerk of the secretariat.
proposals.after: He again became chief clerk to the Minister of Education (Situ).
proposals.reason: 司徒主簿 is the Situ's chief clerk, not a secretariat post.

proposals.before: When his mourning was over he was made left western clerk of the secretariat and attendant administrative officer of the province.
proposals.after: When his mourning was over he was made left western clerk to the Minister of Education (Situ) and attendant administrative officer of the province.
proposals.reason: 司徒左西掾 belongs to the Situ, not the secretariat.

proposals.before: In the twelfth year of Yuanjia the eastern commanderies were flooded and the people starved. In Yixing and Qiantang in Wu, rice reached three hundred cash per sheng.
proposals.after: In the twelfth year of Yuanjia the eastern commanderies were flooded and the people starved. In Wu, Yixing, and Qiantang of Wu commandery, rice reached three hundred cash per sheng.
proposals.reason: 吳義興及吳郡之錢唐 names Wu, Yixing, and Qiantang of Wu commandery.

proposals.before: Ye harbored a treacherous plot; Yanzhi sensed his strangeness and spoke to the Taizu; Ye soon's affair broke out and he was executed.
proposals.after: Ye harbored a treacherous plot; Yanzhi sensed his strangeness and spoke to the Taizu; Ye's affair soon broke out and he was executed.
proposals.reason: Ye soon's is ungrammatical; 尋 modifies the outbreak of the affair.

proposals.before: Early in Emperor Xiaowu's Daming era, Mu was exiled to Shixing for drawing the emperor's attendant Yu Xin into discussions of inner-palace affairs and for feuding with his younger brother Bo, literary attendant to the prince of Xiyang. Bo was dismissed and placed under house arrest.
proposals.after: Early in Emperor Xiaowu's Daming era, Mu was exiled to Shixing for drawing the emperor's attendant Yu Xin into discussions of inner-palace affairs and for feuding with his younger brother Bo, literary attendant to the prince of Xiyang. Bo was dismissed and barred from office.
proposals.reason: 禁錮 means prohibition from holding office (proscription), not confinement under house arrest.

proposals.before: Tong's light service exceeded the norm; the responsible offices memorialized dismissal.
proposals.after: Tong overused his assigned servants beyond the limit; the responsible offices memorialized dismissal.
proposals.reason: 輕役過差 refers to excessive miscellaneous labor imposed on allotted dry servants, not 'light service.'

proposals.before: Shizu issued an edict: "Lately dry servants mostly do not respect their supply—masters may as a measure permit carrying staff."
proposals.after: Shizu issued an edict: "Lately dry servants have mostly failed to attend to their duties; masters may, as a measure, be permitted to apply the staff."
proposals.reason: 行杖 means administering corporal beating with the staff, not carrying a staff; 祗給 is performance of allotted service.

proposals.before: If the two sons had lived out their years, one still would not know where coming calamity would stop.
proposals.after: If the two men had lived out their years, one still would not know where coming calamity would stop.
proposals.reason: 二子 here means the two men just discussed (Wang Hua and Kong Ningzi), not 'sons.'

decisions.reason: 司徒左長史 is the left chief clerk of the Situ, not of the Secretariat; the proposed office name matches the Chinese.
The literal field repeats the same error: 司徒 is the Minister over the Masses, not the Secretariat.
政事悉委司馬張邵 names Zhang Shao as 司馬 (adjutant), distinct from 主簿 in the preceding sentence; chief clerk is the wrong office.
Literal 司馬 should be Adjutant, not Chief Clerk, which would render 主簿.
華陽不知是邵 is 佯不知: Hua feigned not to know it was Shao. Reading 陽 as sunlight invents dazzling and a genuine mistake.
The literal 'in the sunlight' likewise misreads 陽; pretended not to know is the correct sense.
平乘戶 is the cabin door of a large barge, not a place called Pingcheng; the following sentence's boat (舟) confirms the naval setting.

decisions.after: He led the military and civil officials of the headquarters and province in strict array to guard themselves. The various officials dispatched from the court—all could not draw near his ranks. Army Adviser Zhu Rongzi embraced his sword outside the cabin door of the pingcheng barge, not unbuckling his belt for several tens of days.
decisions.reason: Pingcheng gate is wrong, but 'door of the pingcheng barge' is stiff; cabin door of the pingcheng barge keeps 平乘 and 戶 without treating Pingcheng as a gate.
中書舍人 is the secretariat drafter, not an attendant gentleman, a title that overlaps other gentleman-attendant offices.
昇明末 is the Liu Song Shengming era; the English 'Qi Shengming' invents a Qi reign the Chinese does not name.
情事兼常 means the circumstances of feeling exceed the ordinary; 'all the more ordinary' reverses 兼常. 偏罰 is the partial loss of a parent.
丁母憂，葬竟 marks recall after burial while still in mourning; 服闋 'mourning complete' appears only later in s0144.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 丁母憂，葬竟，起為領軍將軍

decisions.reason: 太后所生蘇氏 need not mean a daughter the empress dowager bore; 懿戚 and later kinship language support a kinswoman, so the literal daughter reading over-commits.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 上奉太后所生蘇氏甚謹

decisions.reason: 郡命主簿 is an appointment by the commandery as registrar; it does not mention a commandery prince.
Literal 郡命 is the commandery's appointment, not service to a prince; the repair restores that syntax.
司徒祭酒 is libationer under the Situ, not an office of the imperial secretariat.
復為司徒主簿 returns him as the Situ's chief clerk, not a secretariat post.
司徒左西掾 belongs to the Situ's staff; rendering it as a secretariat clerk is the same 司徒/secretariat confusion.
吳義興及吳郡之錢唐 lists Wu, Yixing, and Qiantang of Wu commandery; collapsing this to 'Yixing and Qiantang in Wu' drops 吳 as a separate place.
曄尋事發伏誅 has 尋 modifying the outbreak of the affair; 'Ye soon's' is ungrammatical and misparses 尋.
勃免官禁錮 is dismissal plus prohibition from office; 禁錮 is not house arrest.
In the 幹僮不得雜役 context, 輕役過差 is excessive labor imposed on allotted servants, not 'light service.'
量聽行杖 authorizes applying the staff; 不祗給 is failure in allotted service, not 'carrying staff' or 'respect their supply.'

sourceWitness.excerpt: 多不祗給，主可量聽行杖

decisions.reason: 若二子永年 refers to the two men just discussed, a standard historian's use of 子, not their sons.

claimRevisions.reason: 華陽不知是邵 is feigned ignorance, so the extracted action 'mistook' was created by the sunlight misreading, not by the Chinese.
